text: Each party agrees that all information disclosed by one party to the other party, whether orally, in writing, or electronically, shall be treated as confidential. Confidential Information shall not include information that: (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving party; (b) was known to the receiving party prior to disclosure; (c) is independently developed by the receiving party without use of the Confidential Information; or (d) is disclosed pursuant to a court order or legal requirement. The receiving party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, advisors, and legal counsel who have a need to know. The obligations of confidentiality shall survive for a period of three (3) years following termination of this Agreement. Upon termination, the receiving party shall return or destroy all Confidential Information and certify such destruction in writing.

The Recipient acknowledges that all proprietary data, trade secrets, business plans, customer lists, and technical specifications provided by the Discloser constitute Confidential Information. The Recipient shall not disclose such information to any third party without the prior written consent of the Discloser. The Recipient agrees that any breach of this section would cause irreparable harm to the Discloser, entitling the Discloser to seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity.

Both parties acknowledge that in the course of performing this Agreement, each party may receive or have access to any and all information, data, documents, materials, trade secrets, and know-how of the other party. Such Confidential Information excludes information that: (i) is in the public domain; (ii) was independently developed without reference to the disclosing party's Confidential Information; or (iii) was received from a third party without restriction. Each party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, affiliates, and professional advisors who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those herein. The obligations under this section shall continue in perpetuity. Upon written request, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy all materials containing Confidential Information. Each party acknowledges that a breach would result in irreparable injury and that the disclosing party shall be entitled to equitable relief, including injunction and specific performance.

Provider shall maintain the confidentiality of Customer Data and shall not disclose Customer Data to any third party except as required by law. Provider shall implement reasonable security measures to protect Customer Data from unauthorized access.

"Confidential Information" means any information disclosed by either party to the other, including but not limited to software, technical data, business strategies, financial information, and customer information. The following shall not constitute Confidential Information: (a) information that becomes publicly known through no wrongful act of the receiving party; (b) information that was in the receiving party's possession before receipt from the disclosing party; (c) information that is independently developed by the receiving party; (d) information that is lawfully received from a third party without restriction. The receiving party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees and subcontractors who need to know such information and who are bound by written confidentiality agreements. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the receiving party shall be free to use for any purpose the residuals resulting from access to the Confidential Information, provided that the receiving party shall not disclose the Confidential Information except as expressly permitted herein. "Residuals" means ideas, concepts, know-how, or techniques that are retained in the unaided memory of the receiving party's personnel. The confidentiality obligations hereunder shall survive for five (5) years from the date of disclosure. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement, each party shall return or destroy all Confidential Information of the other party.

All information provided by Company to Contractor in connection with the Services shall be deemed confidential. Contractor shall not use such information for any purpose other than performing the Services. This confidentiality obligation shall survive the termination of this Agreement indefinitely.

Each party agrees to keep confidential all non-public information received from the other party. The confidentiality obligation does not apply to information that is or becomes publicly available, is already known to the receiving party, is independently developed, or is disclosed under compulsion of law. Either party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, agents, and representatives who have a need to know such information. The obligations set forth in this Section shall survive for a period of two (2) years following the termination or expiration of this Agreement.

Vendor acknowledges that in performing the Services, Vendor may have access to confidential and proprietary information of Client, including without limitation, trade secrets, customer lists, pricing information, marketing strategies, product development plans, and financial data (collectively, "Confidential Information"). Vendor shall hold all Confidential Information in strict confidence and shall not disclose such information to any third party. Vendor may disclose Confidential Information only to its employees who need access to perform the Services and who have signed individual non-disclosure agreements. Upon termination, Vendor shall immediately return all documents and materials containing Confidential Information and shall permanently delete any electronic copies. Vendor acknowledges that unauthorized disclosure would cause irreparable harm and that Client shall be entitled to injunctive relief without the necessity of proving actual damages.

The parties agree that all information exchanged under this Agreement shall be treated as confidential. Neither party shall disclose Confidential Information without prior written consent. This obligation shall not apply to information that: (a) is publicly available; (b) was known prior to disclosure; (c) is received from a third party without obligations of confidentiality; (d) is required to be disclosed by law or governmental order, provided that the receiving party gives prompt notice. The confidentiality obligations under this Agreement shall be perpetual.

Licensee shall maintain in confidence all technical documentation, source code, algorithms, and specifications provided by Licensor. Licensee shall use such information solely for the purpose of exercising its rights under this License Agreement. Licensee shall restrict access to Confidential Information to those of its employees and contractors who need such access and who have executed confidentiality agreements. The foregoing obligations shall not apply to information that becomes publicly available other than through Licensee's breach, or that Licensee can demonstrate was independently developed.

"Confidential Information" shall mean any and all information, whether written, oral, electronic, or visual, disclosed by one party to the other in connection with this Agreement. Confidential Information includes, without limitation, all business plans, financial records, customer data, technical know-how, inventions, processes, and methodologies. The receiving party may share Confidential Information with its employees, affiliates, legal counsel, and accountants who have a need to know and who are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as those set forth herein. The receiving party acknowledges that breach of this provision may cause irreparable injury and agrees that the disclosing party shall be entitled to seek equitable relief, including specific performance and injunctive relief. The obligations of this Section shall survive for seven (7) years after termination of this Agreement. Upon termination or upon request by the disclosing party, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information and certify such return or destruction in writing.

Each party acknowledges that it may receive information that the disclosing party considers confidential. The receiving party agrees to protect such information using the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential information, but in no event less than reasonable care.

Company shall not disclose the terms and conditions of this Agreement to any third party without the prior written consent of Provider, except to Company's legal and financial advisors who need to review the terms in connection with their professional duties. Company acknowledges that breach of this provision shall entitle Provider to injunctive relief.

All information disclosed by either party, including without limitation trade secrets, business information, technical data, and proprietary materials, shall be deemed Confidential Information. The receiving party shall not disclose Confidential Information to any person other than its employees, officers, directors, agents, and professional advisors who have a need to know and are bound by obligations of confidentiality. Confidential Information shall not include: (i) information that is or becomes part of the public domain through no breach by the receiving party; (ii) information that was in the receiving party's possession prior to receipt; (iii) information independently developed without use of the disclosing party's Confidential Information; (iv) information received from a third party who is not bound by confidentiality obligations. Notwithstanding the above, the receiving party's personnel shall be free to use residuals for any purpose. "Residuals" means information retained in the unaided memories of personnel who have had access to Confidential Information. Upon termination, each party shall return or destroy all tangible materials containing Confidential Information. The obligations of confidentiality shall survive for three (3) years after termination.

Consultant agrees not to disclose any confidential or proprietary information of Client obtained during the engagement. This obligation shall continue in perpetuity after the termination of this engagement. Upon completion of the engagement, Consultant shall return all materials and documents provided by Client.

Neither party shall disclose any information designated as "Confidential" by the disclosing party. The receiving party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees and affiliates on a need-to-know basis. This obligation does not extend to information that is publicly available or was independently developed. The obligations under this Section shall survive for one (1) year following termination.

Supplier shall treat as confidential all data, materials, and information provided by Buyer in connection with this Purchase Order. Supplier shall not disclose such information without Buyer's prior written consent. Supplier shall limit access to employees who require such access for the performance of the order. In the event of unauthorized disclosure, Buyer shall be entitled to seek injunctive and other equitable relief. Upon completion of the order, Supplier shall destroy all copies of Buyer's Confidential Information and provide written certification of such destruction within thirty (30) days.

Each party (as "Receiving Party") agrees to hold in confidence all Confidential Information of the other party (as "Disclosing Party"). "Confidential Information" means all information, in any form, disclosed by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party that is designated as confidential or that reasonably should be understood to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Confidential Information does not include information that: (a) is or becomes generally known to the public without breach of this Agreement; (b) was known to the Receiving Party at the time of disclosure as shown by its records; (c) becomes available to the Receiving Party from a source other than the Disclosing Party without breach of any obligation of confidentiality; (d) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, representatives, and legal advisors. The confidentiality obligations shall survive for a period of five (5) years following the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

The Receiving Party agrees to hold in confidence and not to use, except in connection with the Purpose, any Confidential Information disclosed by the Disclosing Party. The Receiving Party shall restrict disclosure of Confidential Information to its employees, agents, and subcontractors who need to know such information. The Receiving Party shall not reverse-engineer any products or materials provided under this Agreement.

The parties mutually agree that any and all information exchanged between them, whether oral, written, or electronic, including all technical, commercial, financial, and operational data, shall constitute Confidential Information. Excluded from this definition is information that: (a) is publicly known at the time of disclosure; (b) becomes publicly known after disclosure through no fault of the Receiving Party; (c) is in the Receiving Party's possession at the time of disclosure without restriction; (d) is obtained from a third party without breach of confidentiality; (e) is independently developed; or (f) is required to be disclosed by law, regulation, or court order, provided that the disclosing party receives prompt written notice. Either party may share Confidential Information with its employees, officers, directors, advisors, affiliates, and subcontractors bound by written confidentiality obligations. Upon termination or expiration, each party shall return or destroy all Confidential Information of the other party and provide written certification of such action. Each party acknowledges that any breach or threatened breach may cause irreparable harm and agrees that the non-breaching party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief. The obligations of this Section shall survive in perpetuity.

Employee agrees to hold in strictest confidence all trade secrets and proprietary information of Employer. Employee shall not, during or after employment, disclose trade secrets to any person or entity. Employee acknowledges that violation of this section would cause irreparable injury to Employer and that Employer shall be entitled to injunctive relief and specific performance in addition to all other remedies. These confidentiality obligations shall survive termination of employment indefinitely.

Each party agrees that all Confidential Information, including without limitation any business, technical, or financial information, disclosed under this Agreement shall be held in confidence. The Receiving Party shall limit disclosure to those of its employees and advisors with a need to know who are bound by confidentiality obligations. Excluded from Confidential Information is information that is publicly available, independently developed, or received from a third party free of restriction. Upon termination, each party shall return or destroy all Confidential Information. The obligations hereunder shall survive for four (4) years from the date of disclosure.

The parties acknowledge that in performing their obligations under this Agreement, each party may disclose confidential and proprietary information to the other. Each party agrees to use such information only for purposes of this Agreement and to protect the confidentiality of such information using commercially reasonable measures.

Receiving Party shall protect the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information with the same degree of care used for its own confidential information. Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, contractors, and legal counsel who need access. The parties agree that their personnel who have had access to Confidential Information shall be free to use for any purpose the residuals resulting from such access, provided that this right does not represent a license under any patent, copyright, or trade secret. For purposes of this section, "Residuals" means ideas, concepts, know-how, or techniques that are retained in the unaided memory of such personnel.

Customer acknowledges that the Software and all related documentation constitute trade secrets and Confidential Information of Provider. Customer shall not disclose, publish, or disseminate such information to any third party. Customer shall restrict access to its employees who require access to use the Software. Upon termination of this License, Customer shall return all copies of the Software and documentation to Provider and delete all electronic copies from its systems within ten (10) business days.

"Confidential Information" means any and all proprietary information, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by inspection, including but not limited to inventions, designs, algorithms, software code, business methods, marketing plans, customer information, pricing data, and financial results. Confidential Information shall not include information that: (a) was in the public domain at the time of disclosure; (b) enters the public domain after disclosure without breach; (c) was rightfully known by the Receiving Party prior to disclosure; (d) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to Confidential Information; or (e) is lawfully disclosed by a third party. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to employees, officers, directors, accountants, attorneys, and financial advisors under obligations of confidentiality. The confidentiality obligations in this Section shall survive for a period of ten (10) years following termination. Upon termination, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy all copies of Confidential Information within thirty (30) days and certify such action in writing. Each party acknowledges that breach may cause irreparable harm and that the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to equitable relief including injunctive relief.

Contractor shall keep confidential all information relating to Client's business operations. Contractor shall not copy or retain any documents or materials belonging to Client beyond the term of this engagement.

Both parties agree that all non-public information shared during the term of this Agreement is confidential. Neither party shall disclose such information except to employees and affiliates with a need to know who are bound by equivalent confidentiality terms. The exceptions to confidentiality include information in the public domain, information independently developed, information lawfully obtained from third parties, and information required to be disclosed by governmental authority. The obligations of confidentiality shall survive for two (2) years following termination or expiration of this Agreement.

Service Provider agrees that any and all information provided by or on behalf of Company, including without limitation all data, records, strategies, processes, methods, customer information, and financial projections, constitutes Confidential Information. Service Provider shall hold Confidential Information in strict confidence and shall not disclose it to any third party without Company's prior written consent. Service Provider may share Confidential Information with its employees and subcontractors who need access to perform the Services and who are bound by written confidentiality agreements. Upon termination, Service Provider shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information and shall certify in writing that all copies have been returned or destroyed. Service Provider agrees that any unauthorized use or disclosure would cause irreparable harm and that Company shall be entitled to immediate injunctive relief. The obligations under this Section shall survive termination of this Agreement in perpetuity with respect to trade secrets and for five (5) years with respect to all other Confidential Information.

Each party acknowledges that the other party's Confidential Information is valuable. The Receiving Party shall not disclose Confidential Information to any person except as expressly permitted herein. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its legal counsel and accountants. Confidential Information excludes information that is publicly available through no fault of the Receiving Party or that is compelled to be disclosed by law. Upon written request, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy all Confidential Information.

Partner A and Partner B each agree that all information shared in the course of the joint venture shall be treated as confidential. Each party shall restrict access to its officers, directors, employees, and advisors who need to know such information. The parties agree that their respective personnel shall be free to use residuals for any purpose, where residuals means general ideas, concepts, or techniques retained in the unaided memory of personnel who have had access to Confidential Information, provided that this does not constitute a license to any intellectual property. The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Section shall survive the termination of the Joint Venture Agreement for a period of three (3) years. Upon termination, each party shall return or destroy all materials containing Confidential Information of the other party. Each party acknowledges that breach of this Section would cause irreparable injury and that the non-breaching party shall be entitled to equitable relief.
Recipient hereby agrees not to disclose any Confidential Information of Discloser. Recipient shall use the Confidential Information solely for evaluating the proposed transaction between the parties.

Each party ("Receiving Party") agrees to maintain in confidence all Confidential Information of the other party ("Disclosing Party"). "Confidential Information" includes any information designated as confidential and any information that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential. Exceptions: (a) public domain information; (b) previously known information; (c) independently developed information; (d) information received from a third party without restriction; (e) information compelled by law with prior notice. The Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, affiliates, and representatives on a need-to-know basis. The Receiving Party shall use no less than reasonable care to protect Confidential Information. The obligations of this Section shall continue for five (5) years from the Effective Date.

Vendor shall maintain the confidentiality of all Customer Data processed under this Agreement. Vendor shall implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect Customer Data. Vendor shall not access Customer Data except as necessary to provide the Services. Vendor shall ensure that its personnel who have access to Customer Data are bound by obligations of confidentiality. Upon expiration or termination, Vendor shall delete all Customer Data within sixty (60) days and provide written confirmation.

The parties agree that any and all information, data, documents, and materials exchanged in connection with this Agreement, including but not limited to technical specifications, business plans, financial statements, pricing models, and customer databases, shall constitute Confidential Information. The following exceptions apply: (i) information in the public domain at the time of disclosure or that subsequently enters the public domain without breach; (ii) information independently developed as evidenced by written records; (iii) information lawfully obtained from a third party without restriction; (iv) information that was in the Receiving Party's possession prior to disclosure as demonstrated by written records; (v) information required to be disclosed by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, provided the Receiving Party gives prompt notice and cooperates with protective orders. Each party may disclose Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, affiliates, subcontractors, and professional advisors who need to know such information and who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those herein. Notwithstanding the foregoing, each party's personnel shall be free to use for any purpose the residuals resulting from access to the Confidential Information of the other party, provided that the foregoing does not constitute a license under any patent, copyright, or other intellectual property right. "Residuals" means ideas, concepts, know-how, or techniques that are retained in the unaided memory of such personnel who have had access to Confidential Information. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement, each party shall promptly return or destroy all materials embodying Confidential Information of the other party and shall provide written certification of such action within thirty (30) days. Each party acknowledges that unauthorized disclosure or use of Confidential Information may cause irreparable harm and agrees that the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive and other equitable relief, including specific performance, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity. The obligations set forth in this Section shall survive in perpetuity with respect to trade secrets and for a period of five (5) years from the date of disclosure for all other Confidential Information.
